# AI Data Sources

## AI Data Sources Overview

**Does Chatty automatically sync my shipping policy, About us, or other store pages?** Yes — Chatty auto-syncs these Shopify store pages with no manual re-sync needed: Shipping policy, Return policy, Privacy policy, Terms of service, FAQ, Contact us, and About us. If a merchant updates one of these pages, the AI picks up the change automatically. No action required.

Data sources are the information you provide to train your AI agent. The AI uses this data to give accurate, personalized responses about your products, services, and policies.

> **The four store sources start switched off.** Products, Collections, Discounts and FAQs are each
> synced into Chatty automatically — but the AI is **not allowed to use any of them until the store
> turns that source on** under **AI agent → Training data**. Syncing and using are
> two separate things, and only the syncing happens on its own.
>
> This is the single most common cause of *"the AI doesn't know my products"*, *"it makes answers
> up"*, or *"it says it can't find anything"*. Always check which sources are switched on before
> looking at anything else — a store can have thousands of products synced and an AI that is not
> permitted to read one of them.

**Store data (auto-synced):**
- Products: descriptions, variants, pricing, availability, inventory status, metafields
- Discounts: all active and inactive discounts from Shopify
- Markets: market settings including currency and exchange rates
- FAQs: your existing FAQs in Chatty

**Custom data (manually added):**
- Questions (Q&A pairs)
- URLs (website links — content is scraped and indexed)
- Files (.JSON, .TXT, .PDF, .CSV — max 2MB for AI training data; images and PDFs with tables not yet supported)

Since **02/09**, FAQs and custom data live together in the single **Knowledge base** tab — see
*Knowledge Base Tab (since 02/09)* below for how it's organized and how each entry's status works.

**Auto-synced Shopify pages:** Shipping policy, Return policy, Privacy policy, Terms of service, FAQ, Contact us, About us. These sync automatically — no manual action needed.

Product information updates daily at **00:00 UTC**. To sync sooner, trigger a manual resync in **AI agent → Training data → Products → Sync products**.

**What "product training" actually does:** Chatty simply **reads** the product data — title, description, price, variants — so the AI can answer questions about it. It does not modify, publish, or unpublish anything in the merchant's store.

---

## Adding & Managing Data Sources

Go to **AI agent** → **Training data**.

Training data is organized into 5 tabs:

- **Products** — enable/disable products for AI training, manage metafields, sync manually
- **Collections** — enable/disable collections; synced automatically with products
- **Discounts** — discount codes and automatic discounts from Shopify; auto sync daily
- **Markets** — market settings, currencies, exchange rates from Shopify
- **Knowledge base** — FAQs (published FAQ library) and custom Q&As/URLs/files together in one table (see below)

After adding data, click **Test AI** (top right) to verify AI responds correctly.

**Bulk management:** Select multiple items for bulk actions: set as active, set as inactive, or delete.

---

## Knowledge Base Tab (since 02/09)

**What changed:** training data that used to be split across two separate tabs — **FAQs** and
**Custom knowledge** — now lives together in one **Knowledge base** tab, in a single table. This
replaces both of the old tabs; there is no more separate "FAQs" or "Custom knowledge" tab under
**Training data**. (The standalone **FAQs** page/FAQ Builder — the storefront-facing FAQ page —
is unaffected; see `faq_faqs-page`. This change is specifically about the AI training data tab.)

**Per-entry status — three states, not just on/off:**
- **Set live** — the AI actively uses this entry to answer customers.
- **Move to draft** — kept in the table but the AI does not use it yet. Useful for reviewing
  content (e.g. auto-generated FAQs) before it goes live.
- **Turn off** — disabled, same as the old Active/Inactive toggle.

**Auto-synced content lands in Draft, not Live.** Anything that comes in automatically (e.g. from
**Sync FAQs** or the **Store pages** sync) is added as **Draft** — a merchant has to review and
set it **Live** themselves before the AI will use it. If a merchant says "I synced my FAQs but the
AI still doesn't know them," check whether the synced entries are sitting in Draft.

**Sync FAQs and Store pages run in the background** — a merchant can navigate away from the tab
while a sync is running and the progress is still tracked; no need to keep the tab open.

**Duplicate content is not silently skipped.** If new content overlaps with an existing entry, the
system asks the merchant to choose: create a new entry, merge with the existing one, or replace it.

**Synced FAQs don't count toward the data source limit.** FAQ content pulled in via sync does not
count against the store's plan data-source limit — only manually added custom entries do.

**Freshness/quality banners:** the table shows a banner nudge when an entry is too short, too long,
or hasn't been updated in **90+ days** — a prompt to review it, not a hard block.

---

## Smart Recommendations Setup

Tell AI which products to recommend in specific situations:

1. Go to **AI agent → Skills → Shopping → Smart recommendations**
2. Select a collection to manage
3. Set up product list and keywords
4. Click **Add product** to add items, **Delete** to remove
5. Click **Save** and activate the recommendation

**System recommendations** (pre-configured, always available):
- **Best sellers** — AI suggests when customers ask "What's popular?" Enable **Activate smart syncing** to auto-select top products based on sales, or add products manually.
- **New arrivals** — AI suggests when customers ask "What's new?" Enable **Activate smart syncing** to auto-populate, or add products manually.

**Custom recommendations** (create your own):
- **Sale promotion** — triggers when customers mention "sale", "discount", "deal". Set search terms + product conditions (add by product or by collection).
- **Special occasions** — triggers when customers mention "gift", "birthday", "anniversary". Set search terms + product conditions.
- Click **Add recommendation** to create additional custom types.

---

## Managing Individual Products

After syncing products:
1. Go to **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Products** tab
2. Set each product's status to **Enabled** or **Disabled**

Only published, in-stock products work with Chatty. Product subscriptions are not supported.

**Add product-specific FAQs (AI training data):**
1. Click **Products** tab
2. Click **Add FAQs** or **Manage FAQs** on a specific product
3. Type each question and answer yourself

These FAQs teach the **AI agent** about that product — they are training data. Write them
manually; the AI-generate option produces FAQs for the store as a whole, not per product.

> To display a different set of FAQs on each **product page of the storefront**, this is the
> wrong tool. Use **FAQs** → **FAQs block**: create a block per product or group, select the
> questions, and set the display condition to **Product pages → by collection/tag**.
> See `faq_faqs-block`.

## Troubleshooting File & URL Training

- **CSV import shows questions as "Failed":** this is usually because the topic was set to **Published but not Active**. Set the topic **Active**, fix the file, and re-upload. If the app won't let you delete the failed rows, contact support to clear them.
- **Adding a website URL only trains the homepage:** entering the **domain alone** trains the AI on the homepage only. To train on specific content, add the **individual page URLs** (e.g. `/pages/avada-faqs`). The AI does **not** auto-scrape your whole site — you choose what to feed it.
- **File limits:** PDF, CSV, TXT, JSON, **max 2 MB each**; CSV is best for structured Q&A. Images and PDFs whose content is in tables/scans may not be parsed — re-enter that data as text.
- **URL/file training stuck "In Progress" or "Failed":** delete and re-add one at a time — a common cause is the source page being **password-protected**, which blocks the crawler (Shopify's own Shipping/Return/FAQ pages are exempt since those are synced directly, not crawled). Workaround: paste the content into a supported file (PDF/CSV/TXT/JSON, 2MB max) and upload under **Knowledge base → Add data → Files** instead.

# AI Training & Setup

> **Since mid-to-late August 2026, AI agent is a hub page**, not one long settings
> screen — every step below (Training data, Instructions, Skills, Scenarios, Settings)
> is its own top-level page reached by clicking its card from **AI agent**, not a tab
> or a "Manage" button inside a longer page.

## Setting Up AI Training for the First Time

To set up your AI agent, follow these steps:

1. Go to **AI agent** → **Training data** to add training data (Products, Collections, Discounts, Markets, Knowledge base)
2. Go to **AI agent** → **Instructions** to add custom instructions for how the AI should respond
3. Go to **AI agent** → **Skills** to turn on what the AI can do (Smart recommendations, Product quiz, Order tracking, Human handover, etc.) and **AI agent** → **Scenarios** for any custom scenario
4. Go to **AI agent** → **Settings** to set the AI name, avatar/logo, welcome message, and re-engagement
5. Click **Test AI** → **Test now** to test responses before going live

Would you like to set this up yourself, or have our team handle the full setup for you, free of charge? They'll train your AI assistant to fit your store, and you can adjust anything afterwards.

**How to answer this:** When a merchant asks how to set up their AI agent, give the setup steps above and the free-setup offer — nothing else. Do **not** add a note that advanced features or data sources require a paid plan; the merchant did not ask about plans, and leading with a paywall discourages setup. Only discuss plans or paid features if the merchant asks about pricing/plans directly, or when a step they want to take needs a feature their current plan doesn't include — at that point name the specific feature and point them to the pricing page. Advanced features that are paid-only: Store Instructions, Scenarios, QnA, and Data Source expansion (this list is for your reference, not for volunteering).

**For high-revenue stores** (ARR > $200K on a paid plan): proactively offer help with initial setup and a demo call with PM.

---

## Restoring Deleted AI Instructions

To recover deleted AI Instructions, contact support team for further help.

---

## Testing AI Responses

Use the built-in **Test** feature — it does **NOT** count against the merchant's AI replies quota.

1. Go to **AI agent** → **Test AI** → **Test now**
2. Enter questions and check AI responses

**Important:** Under the new pricing policy, each plan (except Plus) has limited AI Replies. Do not test directly on the merchant's live chat without permission.

---

## Prevent AI from Sharing Support Email

1. Go to **AI agent** → **Instructions** → **General instructions** → **Behaviours**
2. Add: `Do not provide Store Support Email addresses to customers.`
3. Save the changes
4. Test by asking "How can I contact support?" to confirm the email is no longer shown

---

## Disabling AI Follow-Up Questions

Follow-up questions — the AI suggesting a next question to keep the conversation going — are **off
by default**. A store only sees them if someone turned the *Product question suggestions* scenario on.
Check that first: if a merchant wants them gone, switching that scenario back off is usually all it
takes and they can do it themselves.

If they still appear after that, it has to be switched off for them on our side.

1. Confirm the merchant really wants the AI to answer directly, with no follow-up question
2. Tell them the team will switch it off for them, then hand it over so it can be applied
3. Explain the trade-off: answers get shorter and feel less personal afterwards
4. Once it is done, ask them to test again and confirm it matches what they wanted

---

## AI Showing Wrong Support Email

The AI pulls the support email from **AI agent** → **Settings** → **Support email addresses**.

1. Check which email the AI sent to the customer
2. Go to **AI agent** → **Settings** → **Support email addresses** and check the address set there (separate multiple addresses with commas)
3. If wrong, guide the merchant to update it with the correct one
4. After updating, the AI will automatically use the new email

---

## AI Not Replying to Emails

1. Verify AI email channel is enabled: **AI agent** → **Settings** → **AI Channels** → **Email**
2. AI auto-replies after 5 minutes if no agent responds — only to genuine customer inquiries (not spam or system notifications)
3. If configured correctly but AI still doesn't reply, escalate to the dev team

---

## AI Not Transferring to Human Agents

First check the **Human handover** scenario — edit it at **AI agent → Scenarios → Human handover** (the same setting shows as a **Human agent transfer** status row on **AI agent → Skills → Customer support**; see `faq_human-handover` for the naming note):
- **Auto triggers:** "Customer asks to talk to a person" is always on; "AI cannot answer", "Customer repeats question", and "Negative sentiment" are toggles — confirm the relevant trigger is enabled.
- **Destination:** confirm "Transfer to human in Chatty inbox" is selected (vs. "Collect info & follow up by email" / "Show contact methods").
- **Offline behavior:** if "Allow only outside business hours" / "Allow all the time" is set, AI keeps replying instead of handing off when the team is offline — this is expected.

If handover is configured correctly but the conversation still shows "Unassigned," agent routing is managed in **Automation settings** (check Automatic Assignment / "Reassign conversations"). If still failing, collect conversation details and escalate to TS/dev team.

---

## Hiding Product Preview Card

There is currently **no dedicated app setting** to disable product preview cards. The preview card shares CSS with the "Reply to" element — hiding via CSS would hide both.

- If merchant doesn't want AI to sell → suggest adjusting AI to focus on support skills instead
- If concerned about cluttered UI → explain the CSS limitation
- If they need more control → log feedback and escalate to the product team

---

## AI Responds Before Pre-Chat Form

This happens when customers interact via the **AI Product Assistant** on the product page — it prioritizes quick answers without requiring customer info first.

If the merchant's priority is collecting customer info before any response, they should hide the **AI Product Assistant** on the storefront and rely solely on the pre-chat form.

---

## Creating an AI Scenario

Go to **AI agent** → **Scenarios**, then click **+ Add scenario** and define:

1. **Scenario name** — the topic your customers mention
2. **Instructions** — the messages or flow you want the AI to follow

Use this for returns, order lookups, discount requests, or any specific process you want the AI to handle consistently.

---

## AI Product Sync Limits

| Plan | Product limit |
|------|--------------|
| Free | 200 products |
| Basic | 1,500 products |
| Pro | 8,000 products |
| Plus | Unlimited |

If the store exceeds the plan limit, Chatty trains on the most recently updated products first. For stores with more than 5,000 products, contact support — this requires manual backend configuration.

**After a plan upgrade (fixed 21/08):** the synced-product limit now updates automatically as soon as the upgrade is billed — a store takes whichever is higher between the new plan's limit and whatever was already saved, and the old saved limit is cleared. Previously a store could stay stuck at the old plan's product limit after upgrading; if a merchant reports products still capped right after an upgrade, ask them to re-check — this should no longer happen, and if it still does, treat it as a fresh bug rather than the known old one.

### Bulk Enable/Disable AI Training for Products via CSV Import (20/08)

Merchants no longer have to toggle AI on/off for each product one at a time. **AI agent → Training data → Products → More actions → Bulk edit status** lets a merchant upload a CSV to enable or disable AI training for many products in one pass.

**CSV format:**
- Required columns: **AI Status** (`enabled` or `disabled` per row) and either **id** or **handle** to match the product.
- A Shopify product-export CSV can be used as-is (it already has `id`/`handle`).
- A sample template file is available directly on the upload screen.

**Flow:**
1. Upload the CSV.
2. Before applying, a summary table shows how many products will be enabled, how many disabled, and how many rows were skipped (missing or invalid status value).
3. After confirming, the system reports how many products matched successfully; any unmatched rows can be downloaded as a file to correct and re-import.

**Plan limit still applies:** enabling products via CSV is capped by the store's **AI Product Sync Limits** (see table above) — if the bulk action would push the enabled count past the plan's limit, enabling stops at the plan's maximum rather than enabling everything in the file.

**Confirm button reliability (fixed 21/08):** the **Confirm** dialog for bulk (and single) enable/disable used to hang the screen without completing. This is fixed — Confirm now completes normally, and if the action would exceed the plan's product limit, the dialog explicitly states only a partial number could be added due to the plan limit.

### "It won't upload all my products" / products missing from the list

If products are missing in **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Products**, check in this order:
1. **Deactivated products** — products toggled off in the list won't train; toggle them **Active**.
2. **A search or filter is hiding them** — clear any active search/filter.
3. **Header says "X of X products learned" but the list shows "No items found"** — clear the filter and switch to the **All** tab. If the list is still empty, escalate as a **display bug** (collect store URL + a screenshot).

---

## AI Product Inventory Sync

Chatty syncs product data including inventory status from Shopify. However, **real-time automatic stock quantity updates are not supported**.

To sync the latest data manually: **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Products** → click **Sync products**.

**Out-of-stock products are still learned.** The AI does train on products that are out of stock (as long as they are **Active** in Training data) — it does not skip them. When a customer asks about an out-of-stock item, the AI answers about the product and states that it is currently out of stock; it does not pretend the product doesn't exist. To stop the AI from answering about a specific item entirely, toggle that product **off (Disabled)** in **AI agent → Training data → Products**.

---

## Training Data Language

The AI performs best with training data in the same language your customers use. For multilingual audiences, you can add training data in multiple languages.

Avoid mixing languages in a single FAQ entry — it may reduce accuracy.

---

## Multilingual Product Descriptions

Chatty's AI reads Shopify product descriptions as written. If descriptions are available in multiple languages, the AI can answer in those languages.

For best results, ensure each product has complete descriptions in all supported languages. You can also add multilingual FAQs manually in **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Knowledge base** (since **02/09**, this replaces the old separate **FAQs** tab — see `faq_data-sources` → *Knowledge Base Tab*).

---

## AI Page Context Detection

Yes — Chatty automatically detects the current page URL and product context. When a customer asks a question on a product page, the AI uses that product's information to answer.

Make sure the **Smart recommendations** skill is enabled under **AI agent** → **Skills** → **Shopping** (this skill was renamed from "Product recommendations" — same toggle).

---

## Collection-Based Product Recommendations

Yes — if the AI detects the customer is on a product or collection page, it can use that context to make relevant recommendations.

Make sure **Products** data is enabled in **Training data**. Use collection-specific scenarios to further improve accuracy.

---

## Prevent AI from Sharing Phone Number

1. Go to **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Knowledge base** and remove/replace any phone number mentions with a redirect message: `For phone inquiries, please contact us via email.`
2. Create a **Custom scenario** (**AI agent** → **Scenarios**): `Do not share the store phone number. Direct customers to contact us via email instead.`

---

## AI Shared an Unwanted Private Detail (Address, Personal Email, Other PII)

The AI only shares what's in its training data or settings — trace the source first. Open the offending answer → **Review Sources**; in real cases handled, the source has been either a merchant-added FAQ containing the detail, or the **Support email** field under **AI agent → Instructions**.

1. Remove or edit the entry containing the private detail.
2. Replace it with the contact information the merchant *does* want shared.
3. Add a boundary instruction under **AI agent → Instructions** covering that category of information (e.g. "Never share personal staff contact details or home addresses.").
4. Retest with a few phrasings to confirm it no longer surfaces.

If the merchant can't locate the source themselves, offer to make the change and verify it for them.

---

## Can the AI Read Images or Documents a Customer Sends?

The AI can match a **product photo** a customer sends against the synced catalog and reply about that specific product. It **cannot read or interpret uploaded documents** — PDFs, reports, forms, or other files sent by a customer in chat — and shouldn't be relied on for anything requiring document interpretation. Route those to a human via a **Human handover** intent rule.

(This is separate from a merchant *uploading* a PDF/CSV as training data under **Knowledge base** — see the format table above; that's about feeding the AI's own knowledge, not about the AI reading files customers send mid-chat.)

---

## Best AI Training Content

Include:
- **Accurate product descriptions** with measurements, materials, and key specifications
- **FAQs** covering common questions (shipping, returns, sizing, payments)
- **Custom Scenarios** for specific flows like order status, discount codes, return requests

Keep content clear, avoid conflicting information, and update regularly as products or policies change.

---

## Size Recommendation Setup

**Size guide is a built-in default scenario now** — turn it on at **AI agent → Skills →
Shopping → Size guide**, or edit its content at **AI agent → Scenarios → Size guide**.
It's gated to **Pro or Plus** (the in-app upgrade badge on this row reads "Advanced
plan" — that's just the badge wording, the actual plan requirement is Pro/Plus, same
tier as Product quiz).

Make sure product descriptions include clear size/measurement information — the built-in
scenario references your existing size chart content.

**If a merchant wants trigger phrasing beyond the built-in scenario** (e.g. a specific
brand-voice response), add a separate **Custom Scenario** at **AI agent → Scenarios →
+ Add scenario** with triggers like `what size`, `size guide`, `how does it fit`, and
instructions guiding the AI to refer to the size chart or the size guide page.

---

## AI Giving Wrong Product Links

This usually means the AI matched a query to incorrect backend data (e.g., a collection lookup). Contact support with the **conversation ID** — the team will add an instruction hook to fix the response logic.

As a preventive step, ensure product descriptions are detailed and unambiguous.

---

## Product FAQs and "View Similar" Recommendations

No — product FAQs do **not** influence the "View Similar" recommendation feature. Recommendations are handled through **Smart Recommendations** settings, not FAQ data.

---

## Plan Product Limit Too Low

Each plan has a product sync limit (Free: 200, Basic: 1,500, Pro: 8,000, Plus: Unlimited). If you've hit the limit:

- Contact support and share what you need — the team will review and confirm if a one-time extension is possible (subject to approval)
- For permanent higher limits, upgrade your plan
- If you have more than 5,000 products, contact support directly — this requires manual backend configuration

---

## AI Using Wrong Store's Catalog

Contact support with the **conversation ID**. This is typically caused by the AI matching against backend collection data incorrectly. The team will add an instruction hook to prevent this behavior.

**Milder version — AI references product counts/categories that don't match what's actually synced, but the catalog is still the merchant's own store:** the same fix applies. Contact support with the **conversation ID** so the team can trace why the AI's referenced numbers diverge from **AI agent → Training data → Products**; don't assume it's the wrong-store issue above just because the catalog is stale-looking.

---

## AI and Website Content

**Note:** This applies to external websites only. Shopify store pages (About us, Shipping policy, Return policy, Privacy policy, Terms of service, FAQ, Contact us) are automatically synced — no URL submission needed for these.

For external websites: No — the AI does **not** automatically read your website. You must submit specific page URLs to the **Knowledge base** section (**AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base**, as a URL entry).

Submitting just the domain (e.g., `yourstore.com`) only trains on the homepage content — submit individual page URLs for full coverage.

---

## What AI Model Does Chatty Use — Can I Use OpenAI / Switch the Model?

Chatty runs on a **secure, enterprise-grade large language model built for support**, upgraded regularly. The specific underlying model is not publicly disclosed, and the AI agent layer on top of it is optimized for e-commerce support scenarios.

**There is no option to plug in OpenAI or swap the underlying model** — not on any plan.

**If a merchant feels the replies are weak, the fix is almost always data/instruction quality, not the model:**
1. Turn on the relevant **Skills** — **AI agent → Skills**
2. Tighten the **General instructions** (**AI agent → Instructions**) and add **Custom scenarios** (**AI agent → Scenarios**) for the cases they're unhappy with
3. Add content in **Knowledge base** for anything the AI is missing
4. Re-test in **AI agent → Test AI → Test now** with the exact question that failed

Ask for the **specific example** that disappointed them — that is what makes the fix possible, and it's what the product team needs.

**Log the OpenAI / model-choice request as a feature request** with the merchant's use case and their example.

---

## AI Responding in Wrong Language

The AI is designed to respond in the customer's language. If it's getting confused (especially for very short or ambiguous messages), contact support with the **conversation ID**. The team can add an explicit instruction: `Always reply in the same language the customer is using.`

---

## AI Repeating Auto-Reply FAQ Content

This is a **known bug**. Contact support with the **conversation ID** — the dev team can investigate and fix the response logic so the AI does not repeat content already shown in the auto-reply.

---

## Suppressing Add-to-Cart Button

Scenario Instructions can set behavioral guidelines, but the Add-to-Cart button is a **system-level behavior** — it cannot be suppressed via scenario alone.

Contact support — the team can apply a custom instruction or CSS/code solution.

---

## AI Always Providing Contact Phone Number

Two approaches:
1. Add the phone number to **General AI Instructions** so the AI references it broadly
2. Create a **Custom Scenario** (**AI agent** → **Scenarios** → **+ Add scenario**) triggered when customers ask about contacting the team

---

## AI Points to a Generic Contact Page / Wrong Contact URL

**Symptom:** the AI replies with a vague *"you can reach us via our contact page"* — with the wrong link, or no link at all.

**Fix:** add the merchant's **exact contact URL** to **AI agent → Instructions → General instructions** (or to **Knowledge base**), so the AI references the right page instead of guessing. Re-test in **AI agent → Test AI**.

**If the merchant wants an on-store form rather than a link:**
- Chatty has a **built-in Contact form** section — it displays when a customer requests human/after-sales support. Submissions land in the **Inbox** and are also forwarded to the address set in **AI agent → Settings → Contact support email**.
- Chatty also integrates with **Powerful Contact Form** — set up in **Settings → Integrations** (see `faq_powerful-contact-form`). Each submission becomes a conversation in the inbox.

---

## AI and Loyalty Points / Customer Account Data

No — Chatty AI **cannot** access customer account data (login status, loyalty points balance, etc.).

As a workaround, create a **Custom Scenario** that directs customers to your login/registration page when they ask about rewards or account-specific questions.

---

## Custom Scenario Character Limit

Currently the character limit for individual scenario fields **cannot be increased**. Contact support — the team can help optimize and shorten the scenario text to fit within the limit.

**This is different from the Instructions field cap** (AI agent → Instructions → General instructions): that field has a **~1,000-character limit and support cannot raise it** — an overloaded prompt risks the AI drifting or hallucinating. If a merchant is out of room in Instructions, suggest moving facts out instead: Instructions should describe *behaviour* (tone, boundaries, routing); product details, policies and reference info belong in **Training data → Knowledge base**, which has a far more generous limit.

The **welcome/offline chatbox message fields** are a third, separate cap that is fixed and cannot be raised — see `faq_chatbox-settings.md`.

---

## AI and Shopify Metafields

Only **standard / supported** metafield types are synced to the AI. You can see and toggle which metafields are synced at **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Products** → **Manage metafields**.

**Not supported:** Non-standard / third-party **custom metafields** (for example, metafields created via a separate metafields app) are **not currently synced** — only the supported metafield types sync. Metaobject references (metafields that reference other metaobjects) are also not yet fully supported.

**Workaround:** Add that data into **Knowledge base** as a Q&A so the AI can still use it. If supporting a specific metafield type matters to the store, log a **feature request** with the merchant's use case so the product team can prioritize it.

---

## AI Says "No Access" to Product Specs, Size Charts, or FAQ Metafields

When the AI replies "I don't have access to that information" even though the data is on your product pages, work through these:

1. Confirm the product is **Active** in **AI agent → Training data → Products** and that sync has finished (it can lag a few minutes after install/upload).
2. Standard product fields (title, description, variants, price, availability) and **supported metafields** sync — toggle them in **Products → Manage metafields**. However, **product-page "FAQ" / spec metafields and many third-party/custom metafields are not reliably indexed today**, so technical specs stored only in those tabs may not reach the AI. Re-enter those facts as text in **Knowledge base** (Q&A) or a CSV.
3. **Images are not read.** A **size chart saved as an image won't be parsed** — re-enter that data as text in Knowledge base or a CSV; don't rely on an image.
4. For FAQ/Q&A content, make sure the topic is **Active** and the question is phrased plainly.

As a catch-all, put the missing facts into **Knowledge base** and re-test in **Test AI**. If correctly-synced data still isn't used, send the **conversation ID** so the team can trace it (FAQ/custom-metafield sync is a known coverage gap and can be logged as a feature request).

## Uploading Files for AI Training

Go to **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Knowledge base** → **Add data** → **Files**.

| Format | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| PDF | Supported; not ideal for structured data |
| CSV | **Recommended** for product catalogs and structured Q&A |
| TXT | Supported |
| JSON | Supported |

- Max file size: **2MB per file**
- For large product catalogs → CSV gives better results than PDF
- AI uses RAG — similar customer questions match the closest trained entry

---

## AI Language Switching / Wrong Language Response

1. Go to **Settings → Translation** → confirm the correct **default language** is set
2. Go to **AI agent** → **Instructions** → **General instructions** → **Behaviours** → add:
   > *"Always respond in the same language as the customer."*
3. For real-time translation between agent and customer in the inbox → requires **Pro or Plus plan**

> Free/Basic plans: AI responds based on training data language + customer input. Explicit instruction in step 2 is the most effective fix.

---

## Setting AI Brand Voice / Tone

Go to **AI agent** → **Instructions** → **General instructions** → **Communication style** or **Behaviours**, and add brand tone guidelines. Examples:

- *"You are a friendly assistant for [Brand]. Use warm, casual language."*
- *"Never say 'I apologize' — say 'I'm sorry' instead."*
- *"Write in UK English. Use formal but approachable language."*
- *"Keep responses concise — no more than 3 sentences unless the question requires detail."*

Many merchants skip the Instructions setup entirely — if AI sounds generic, this is the first thing to configure.

---

## Setting Boundaries for the AI (Topics It Should Avoid)

To stop the AI from discussing a topic — pricing exceptions, refunds, competitor mentions, medical/legal claims, anything a merchant wants off-limits — go to **AI agent → Instructions → General instructions → Boundaries** and add an instruction, e.g.: *"Do not offer, confirm, or negotiate refunds or pricing exceptions — redirect the customer to [support contact] instead."*

This is a **separate field from Behaviours**: Behaviours shapes *how* the AI talks (tone, conversation style); **Boundaries defines what it won't talk about** and where it should redirect the customer instead. If a merchant asks "give me boundaries for the AI," "how do I set limits for the AI," or "stop the AI from talking about X," this Boundaries field is the answer — not Behaviours.

For a topic tied to a specific customer flow (e.g. only block refund talk mid-return-request), a **Custom Scenario** (**AI agent → Scenarios → + Add scenario**) can be a stronger, more targeted guardrail than a general Boundaries instruction — the two aren't mutually exclusive.

---

## Disabling AI Product Recommendations

**Option 1 — Toggle Smart Recommendations off:**
Go to **AI agent** → **Skills** → **Shopping** → **Smart recommendations** → Toggle **OFF**

**Option 2 — Custom Instruction:**
Go to **AI agent** → **Instructions** → **General instructions** → **Boundaries** and add: *"Do not recommend products unless the customer explicitly asks for a recommendation."*

> Product recommendations is a **Pro+ feature**. On lower plans, AI uses general product sync — disable via Behaviours instructions.

---

## Changing AI Bot Name / Welcome Message / Avatar

The AI's **display name** — the name customers see on the AI's messages — is set at
**AI agent** → **Settings** → **Name**. The avatar and welcome message live in the same
place, under **AI agent** → **Settings** → **AI identity**.

Tone and self-description are configured separately, at **AI agent** → **Instructions** →
**Manage** → **General instructions**:

- **Role** → describe who the assistant is and how it presents itself (max 250 chars)
- **Communication style** → choose Friendly / Professional / Empathetic / Custom
- **Behaviours** → customize conversation style (max 1000 chars)
- **Boundaries** → its own field, separate from Behaviours — set topics the AI should avoid discussing (e.g. pricing exceptions, refunds) and how it should redirect those topics instead

Changes apply immediately. No republishing required.

> **Behaviours vs. Boundaries:** Behaviours shapes *how* the AI talks (tone, conversation style); Boundaries defines *what it won't* talk about and where it hands off instead. If a merchant asks "how do I stop the AI from promising X" or "set limits for the AI," point them to **Boundaries**, not Behaviours.

> Editing **Role** changes how the AI describes itself, not the name shown on its
> messages. To rename the assistant, change **AI agent → Settings → Name**.
> See `faq_ai-agent-settings` for the full breakdown.

---

## AI Capabilities & Limits (What It Can and Cannot Do)

For feasibility questions — "can the AI do X for us" — Chatty's AI agent **can**: answer from trained product/FAQ/custom content, do guided product recommendations, run scenario-based flows (**AI agent → Scenarios**), hand off to a human via **Human handover** (**AI agent → Scenarios → Human handover**, also shown as **Human agent transfer** on **AI agent → Skills → Customer support**), and — since **13/08** — take two limited actions directly on an order/customer record when the merchant has turned them on at **AI agent → Skills → Customer support** (see `faq_ai-agent-settings` → *AI Agent Actions*): updating the shipping address on an unshipped order, and toggling a customer's marketing email subscription.

**It cannot:**
- Call third-party APIs at runtime (beyond Chatty's own built-in integrations)
- Generate documents (PDFs, contracts, invoices, etc.)
- Host or join live video sessions
- Handle account-level authentication flows inside the chat (login, OTP, password reset) — this includes resetting a customer's password; a "Send password reset" capability was tested but removed on **18/08** and is not available

If a merchant's request needs any of the above, tell them upfront it's out of scope rather than promising a workaround — log it as a feature request if it's a recurring ask.

# Adding and Managing FAQ Questions

## How to Add a New Question

After creating a category, you can add questions to it.

1. Go to **FAQs**
2. Click **Add new** → **Add FAQ**
3. Enter the question and answer
4. Configure settings:
   - **Status**: Published or Draft
   - **Category**: Select which category this question belongs to (required)
   - **Featured question**: If enabled, the question shows on the first page of the chatbox
5. Click **Save**

## How to Manage Questions

- **Edit a question**: Hover over it and click the edit icon
- **Delete a question**: Hover over it and click the delete icon
- **Reorder questions**: Drag and drop within a category
- **Feature/unfeature**: Star or unstar the question

---

## Import FAQs in Bulk

You can import many questions at once using a CSV file.

**Get the sample file:**
Go to **FAQs** → **More actions** → **Import FAQs** → Download the sample CSV

**Fill in the CSV file:**
The file has 5 required fields (keep headers):
- Question
- Answer
- Category (name of the category the question belongs to)
- Published question: TRUE = published, FALSE = unpublished
- Featured question: TRUE = featured, FALSE = not featured

This CSV file is for importing FAQ questions only (not AI training data) — max file size: 1MB.

**Upload the file:**
Click **Import FAQs** → Drop your CSV file → Choose options:
- Overwrite FAQs that have the same questions
- Publish all new categories

## Export FAQs

Go to **FAQs** → **More actions** → **Export FAQs** → Select which FAQs to export → Click **Export**

The export file contains 7 fields: Question, Answer, Category, Published question, Featured question, Published category, Featured category.

## FAQ Formatting / Spacing Looks Broken on the Storefront

Line breaks and spacing added in the FAQ editor don't always render on the storefront, and bullets can sit off to the left — a known rich-text limitation.

- Use **plain text** rather than pasted HTML.
- For consistent spacing/indentation across all FAQs, this is best fixed with a small **CSS adjustment from support** — share your FAQ page URL and the team applies it.
- Logged as product feedback. Alternative: disable Chatty's FAQ page and instead feed your own FAQ page URL into **AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base**.

# FAQs Page

## FAQs Page Overview

The FAQs page is a dedicated page on your Shopify store where customers can browse and find answers without contacting support.

### Why the FAQ page looks blank / "wiped" after upgrading

Upgrading your plan does **not** delete your FAQ content. Two things create this impression:
1. **The Shopify page editor shows the FAQ page as blank by design** — the content is rendered by the Chatty app, not stored in the Shopify page. Check the live storefront URL (`/pages/avada-faqs`) instead of the page editor.
2. **On a new install, Chatty seeds a small sample/default FAQ** as a starting point, which can be mistaken for your real FAQs being replaced.

Your own questions live in **FAQs** → **Manage FAQs** — edit or add them there. The Chatty FAQ page is optional; if you already have your own FAQ page, keep it and feed its URL into **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Knowledge base** instead.

### Can I keep FAQs hidden from the storefront but still have the AI answer them?

Yes — the reverse workflow. Add the questions under **AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base** only, and don't add them to the FAQ page or any FAQ block. The AI uses them in chat and customers never see them as a browsable list.

### "The FAQs page URL has already been taken" / the FAQ page won't activate

This happens when a Shopify page already exists at that path — often a leftover from a previous install, or a page deleted and recreated. Check **Shopify Admin → Online Store → Pages** for a page using the same handle and remove or rename it, then re-enable the FAQ page in Chatty. If it persists, escalate with the store URL — the team can change the URL from their side.

## How to Set Up the FAQs Page

1. Go to **FAQs** → **FAQs page**
2. Toggle on **Display FAQs page**
3. Copy the **FAQs page URL shown in the app** (it is configurable, so do not assume a fixed slug) and add that exact URL to your store navigation
4. Under **Appearance** → **Header**: customize Heading, Description, and optionally toggle on Banner
5. Under **Contact us**: toggle on **Display contact us** to let customers contact your team from the FAQ page
6. Under **Advanced settings**: add **Custom CSS** to match your store's design. Contact support via live chat if you need help styling.

> **Note:** App Embed must also be enabled — click **Turn on** at the top of the page if it shows "Off".

## FAQ Page Font Doesn't Match the Theme, and/or Flagged in a PageSpeed Audit

These two complaints share one fix — always answer both together, even if the merchant only mentions one:

1. **Fix the font mismatch:** go to **FAQs → Appearance → Font** and switch to **"Default"** to inherit the theme font instead of an explicit Google Font. This also removes the extra font-loading request that a PageSpeed/CLS audit can flag.
2. **If a PageSpeed/CLS report still flags a Google Fonts request after that:** it is not Chatty — Chatty loads its own fonts non-blocking via fonts.bunny.net, never Google Fonts. Verify the source before assuming it's Chatty; it can come from a **different app's** custom font `@import` (e.g. Klaviyo has been the actual source in at least one case).

## FAQ Status Changes Not Applying — Check Chat Focus Mode

If **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Chat focus mode** is on, the chatbox skips the Home screen (where the FAQ block lives) entirely — so toggling an FAQ Published/Draft, or reordering categories, never gets a chance to render even though the change saved correctly. Turn Chat focus mode off to confirm the FAQ block itself is working before troubleshooting further as a display bug.

## Review Auto-Generated FAQ Content Before Publishing

FAQs created via **Sync Store Page** or **Generate with AI** are drafts, same as anything added manually — review the question and answer text before publishing. In at least one real case, an auto-generated FAQ surfaced a merchant's personal home address that shouldn't have been customer-facing.

**If a published FAQ exposes information you didn't intend to share:** set it to **Inactive** immediately under **FAQs → Manage FAQs**, then send us the specific entry so we can review why the generation logic surfaced it.

## Set Up the Contact Us Section

The Contact us section on the FAQs page lets customers reach your team when they need more help.

1. In **FAQs** → **FAQs page** → **Contact us** → toggle on **Display contact us**
2. This allows customers to contact you via chatbox or email directly from the FAQ page

## Advanced Settings

- **Custom CSS**: Add custom styling to match your store's design. Contact support via live chat in the app if you need help.

---

## How to Add the FAQs Page to Your Store Navigation

**Main menu:**
1. In Shopify admin, go to **Content** → **Menus** → **Main menu**
2. Click **Add menu item**
3. Name it (e.g., "FAQs")
4. In the link box, search for "Frequently Asked Questions" or paste your custom URL
5. Click **Add** → **Save menu**

**Footer menu:**
Follow the same steps using **Footer menu** instead of Main menu.

**If the merchant cannot do this themselves after the first guide**, follow the collaborator access flow (`ref_collaborator-access.md`) — ask permission, collect the collaborator code, and escalate to TS to handle it directly.

# Suggested Q&A

## What Suggested Q&A Is

Suggested Q&A is the fastest way to give a new AI agent something to work with. Instead of the
merchant writing custom answers from a blank page, Chatty proposes a fixed set of **15 questions
every store gets asked**, drafts an answer for each one from what it already knows about the store,
and lets the merchant accept, edit or skip them one at a time.

Find it at **AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base** — when suggestions are waiting, a banner reading *"N suggested Q&As waiting for review"* appears at the top with a **Review now** button that opens the review page. It is not a card on the AI agent hub, so don't tell a merchant to look for a "Suggested Q&A" menu item. Closing the review page returns to Knowledge base, where accepted answers land.

This is the right thing to point a merchant at when they say the AI does not know basic things about
their store, when they ask "where do I even start with training", or when they have installed the app
and have no custom answers at all yet.

## The 15 Questions

They are grouped into five areas:

**Store info & contact (4)**
- What are your store/support hours?
- How can I contact customer support?
- What payment methods do you accept?
- Which countries do you ship to?

**Shipping & delivery (4)**
- How long does delivery take?
- Do you offer free shipping?
- How can I track my order?
- Do you ship internationally?

**Orders & modifications (3)**
- Can I change or edit my order after placing it?
- Can I cancel my order?
- What if I received a wrong or damaged item?

**Returns & refunds (3)**
- What is your return policy?
- How do I start a return?
- When will I receive my refund?

**Account (1)**
- Do I need an account to place an order?

The list is fixed — merchants cannot add their own questions to it. Anything beyond these 15 goes in
as a normal custom answer under Training data.

## How a Merchant Works Through It

1. Chatty generates a draft answer for each question, pulling from the store's existing settings and
   pages where it can (for example, support hours come from the chat availability settings).
2. Each question sits in one of three states: **waiting for review**, **accepted**, or **skipped**.
3. The merchant reviews each draft, edits anything that is not right, and accepts it. Accepted
   answers become part of what the AI uses.
4. Skipped questions stay skipped and are not used.

Nothing is used by the AI until it has been accepted — a merchant who generated the set but never
reviewed it has gained nothing yet. That is worth checking when someone says "I already did the
suggested questions but the AI still doesn't know".

## Common Situations

**"The drafted answers are wrong or generic."** Expected for anything the store has not configured.
Chatty falls back to a safe generic sentence when it cannot find a real source. The merchant should
edit those before accepting, not accept them as-is.

**"Generation failed / is still running."** Generation runs in the background and can finish, fail,
or still be in progress. If it has failed, it can simply be run again. If it is stuck for a long
time, collect the store URL and hand it over.

**"Can I regenerate after updating my store info?"** Yes — regenerating redrafts the answers.
Answers the merchant already edited and accepted are theirs; check with them before regenerating so
their edits are not lost.

# Test and Optimize AI

## AI Test Zone

You can test your AI agent without enabling it for customers. The test zone simulates customer interactions so you can verify responses before going live.

**Before testing, make sure you've:**
- Added data sources (FAQs, product info, etc.)
- Added custom instructions (tone, voice, response length)
- Set up other settings (bot name, avatar)

There are two ways to test:
- **Test now** — chat with the AI in real time, one question at a time
- **Test with batch** — run a full set of scenarios at once to measure precision, reliability, and helpfulness across multiple cases

**To access:**
Go to **AI agent** → **Test AI** → choose **Test now** 

**How to use Test now:**
1. In the chatbox, ask questions as if you were a customer
2. Use the provided question examples (click **Regenerate questions** for more) — these sample questions exist only to help you test quickly in the test zone; they are **not** shown to customers on the live store
3. Check each response carefully

**What to check:**
- Is the information correct?
- Is the tone friendly but professional?
- Are product details accurate?
- Are prices and availability correct?
- Is the response length appropriate (not too long or too short)?

**Testing tips:**
- Test one topic at a time
- Ask the same question in different ways
- Try edge cases and unusual phrasings

You can also review which data sources the AI used to answer each question.

---

## Improving AI Responses

If the AI gives wrong or incomplete answers, update the training data:

1. Go to **AI agent** → **Training data** → **Knowledge base** → **Questions**
2. Add the question with the correct answer, or edit the existing entry if it is already there
3. For product or collection facts, update the relevant data source under **Training data** instead
4. Go back to **AI agent** → **Test AI** → **Test now** and ask the same question to verify

## AI Response Review

The **Review sources** button showing what data an AI reply used is available in **both places**:

- **In Test AI** — appears under each test reply while you're testing
- **On live customer conversations** — open the conversation in the **Inbox**, find the AI reply in question, and click **Review sources** on that message to see exactly what content it pulled from and where to go edit it

Use this to:
- Add missing product information
- Correct inaccurate policy details
- Expand on partial answers
- Add question variations that weren't understood

**What to do when you spot a problem:**
1. Click **Add relevant data** in the response (Test AI), or open the source shown via **Review Sources** and edit it directly (Inbox)
2. You'll be redirected to data sources to add or fix the right information
3. Watch for patterns — if you're repeatedly adding the same type of info, create comprehensive entries on that topic

---

## Does the AI Learn on Its Own From Customer Conversations?

No. The AI only answers from the training data it's been given — it does not automatically absorb new facts from live chats or from a merchant's own replies to customers.

What it does collect is **Unresolved questions** — things customers asked that it couldn't answer. The review loop:
1. Check **Unresolved questions** regularly (surfaced in the AI agent dashboard).
2. Turn the important ones into Q&A entries under **Training data → Knowledge base**.
3. Retest in **Test AI** to confirm the gap is closed.

This test → find gap → add data → retest loop is how the knowledge base actually improves over time — not passive learning from chat volume.

# Inbox

## Chatty Inbox Overview

The Inbox is your central hub for managing all customer conversations across all connected channels — live chat, email, Facebook Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp — in one place.

**Access inbox:** Go to Chatty in Shopify admin → click the **Inbox** tab.

**Reply to a conversation:**
1. Select a conversation from the list
2. Click the message input field at the bottom
3. Type your message → press **Enter** or click **Send**

For AI-assigned conversations: click **Join conversation** to start responding. You can reassign to AI anytime for auto-reply to resume.

**Filter conversations by:**
- Status: Open, Resolved, Starred, Blocked, Unread
- Channel: Online store, Live chat, Email, Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp
- Assignee: Your inbox, Unassigned, or a specific team member

**While chatting you can see:**
- Contact info, order history, customer tags and notes
- Pages they've browsed
- Real-time behaviors: viewing FAQs, adding/removing products from cart, placing an order

---

## Who a Conversation Gets Assigned To

**Automatic assignment is on by default.** The first team member to reply to a conversation becomes
its assignee, and it stays with them. Nothing is shared out in rotation and nobody is skipped for
being offline unless the store changes those options under **Settings** → **Automation** →
**Assignment method**.

That default explains most of *"why did this land on my colleague?"* — they answered first. It also
explains a member seeing fewer conversations than they expect: once a conversation has an assignee,
it leaves the unassigned queue.

---

## Starting a New Conversation From the Admin (Outbound)

You can proactively start a conversation with a customer from the inbox — you don't have to wait for them to message you first.

**How to create one:**
1. In the **Inbox**, click the **`+`** icon at the top right of the conversation list.
2. In the **Create conversation** popup, fill in:
   - **Email** — the customer's email address (required)
   - **Participants** — optional, up to 5 additional email addresses to include on the thread
   - **Subject of the email** — optional subject line
3. Click **Create**, then type your message and send.

This is an **email conversation** — your message is delivered to the customer's email address, and their replies thread back into your Chatty inbox.

---

## "Send Email" Button Missing When I Start a Conversation Myself

This is expected — it's not a bug.

When you **reply to an existing conversation**, the **"Send email"** button appears because Chatty needs you to confirm which channel that reply goes out on (the customer may have reached you via web chat, Messenger, etc.).

When you **start a new conversation yourself** via the **`+` → Create conversation** flow, you already entered the customer's **email and subject** in the popup, so the channel is set to **email** from the start. Everything you send in that thread goes to the customer's email automatically — there's no separate "Send email" button to click.

**In short:** an admin-initiated conversation created with the customer's email *is* an email conversation. Your messages are emailed to the customer; the missing button just means the email channel is already selected for you.

---

## Anonymous Users Showing Random Names

When a visitor hasn't given their details, Chatty needs some label to identify the conversation in the inbox. Merchants can choose between three display modes at **Settings → Chat appearance → Inbox settings**:

1. **Random names** (default) — a random label like "Grateful dream" or "thunder flake".
2. **Fixed anonymous label** — the visitor shows as "Anonymous-xxx" instead of a random name.
3. **Sequential numbers** — visitors are labeled in order, e.g. "Visitor #1", "Visitor #2".

Two other things CS can do:
- **Remove the `{{customer_name}}` variable** from the AI welcome message (**AI agent → Settings → AI identity → Welcome message**) — the visitor label then only appears in the inbox, never spoken to the customer.
- If the merchant wants to capture real names instead, suggest enabling the **pre-chat form** (**Chatbox → Shared chatbox settings → Pre-chat form**) with Name set as required.

---

## Blocked Customers Starting New Conversations

Blocking in Chatty is currently **session-based** and does not permanently prevent a visitor from starting a new conversation.

For more persistent control:
- Block by IP address (if your store platform supports this)
- Use **Shopify customer tags** to flag or manage abusive customers

The dev team is researching improvements to this feature.

---

## Blocking Visitors by Country

Chatty doesn't currently support blocking all visitors from a specific country at once.

You can block individual visitors — open the conversation, click on the visitor profile, and select **Block**.

For country-level restrictions, consider using **Shopify's geo-blocking features** or a third-party geolocation app.

---

## Stopping Spam / Bot Traffic

Chatty **does** run automated spam detection on incoming messages — this isn't a bare live-chat inbox with no filtering.

**As of 14/08, suspected spam is flagged, not blocked, by default.** Previously, a message the filter flagged as spam had its conversation blocked outright — but the filter isn't perfect, and real customers were getting caught (examples the team traced: a customer typing their own name and email, a customer complaining in English, a German-language question misread as profanity). Now, by default, a flagged conversation is just **marked as spam** in the Inbox and keeps running normally — it is not cut off. Automatic blocking can still be turned on for a store that wants the stricter behavior; if a merchant asks for that, escalate to support to enable it since the exact setting location isn't self-serve documented yet.

What else helps with spam/bot traffic:
- Enable the **pre-chat form** (**Chatbox → Shared chatbox settings → Pre-chat form**) requiring name and email — the friction removes most automated traffic.
- Block at the platform or CDN level if the traffic comes from identifiable sources.
- **Resolve** or **Delete** spam-marked conversations in the Inbox to keep it clean (blocking a specific visitor is separately available and is session-based — see above).
- If spam is inflating AI conversation usage, set a spending cap under **Subscription → View details → Change limit** while working on a longer-term fix.

A full CAPTCHA option is still logged as a feature request.

---

## Reassigning Conversation Back to AI

In the Inbox, open the conversation and look for the assign/reassign option — select the **AI agent** as the assignee.

Note: the customer must send a **new message** after reassignment for the AI to start handling the conversation again.

---

## Replying as Yourself (Not as Admin)

Each team member should log in with their own Chatty account.

If replies are showing as "Admin," check **Settings** → **Automation** — the assignment rule may be keeping conversations assigned to the admin. Change the setting to **"Assign to whoever replies"** to resolve this.

---

## Multiple Shopify Stores

**A unified inbox across several stores exists, and it is a Plus-plan feature.** On Plus, a member
can connect their other stores and work all of their conversations from one inbox, up to **10
connected stores** (the main store is not counted towards that ten).

On Free, Basic and Pro there is no unified inbox: each store has its own Chatty and the merchant
signs into each one separately. That is the correct answer for most merchants asking — but never
answer that the feature does not exist, because on Plus it does.

**Connecting a second store to the same account:** Install Chatty on the second store and, when activating the web app account, click **Activate** to link it to your existing account. You can then switch between stores from the web app (app.meetchatty.com) using the **store switcher in the top-left corner**.

**Limitations:** Each store keeps its own separate inbox and its own plan — conversations are not merged. On mobile, you only receive notifications for the store you're currently switched to (the store name is not shown in the notification). Workaround: use a separate device per store.

---

## Mark All as Read

A "Mark all as read" feature is **not available yet**. This has been submitted as a feature request to the product team.

---

## Exporting Conversation History

Currently, Chatty supports exporting **individual conversations** only — open the conversation → click the **⋮ menu** (top right) → **Export transcript** to download that conversation.

Bulk export with a date range filter is not available in the app UI. If you need to export multiple conversations, contact support with the date range and the team can export the data and send it to your email.

**Exportable fields:** conversation ID, country, language, channel, page the chat started on, message timestamps, sender type, order ID/amount/payment method (if linked to an order).
**Not tracked/exportable:** UTM source/medium/campaign, device/browser/OS, payment or refund/dispute status (those live in Shopify, not Chatty).

---

## Migrating Data to a New Store

Automatic store-to-store migration is **not supported**. Conversation history is tied to the specific store (not the account or domain), so it cannot be transferred even with the same login email or domain — a new store starts fresh.

You can manually copy your **AI Instructions, Scenarios, and FAQ/Q&A content** to the new store. Widget and chatbox settings must be reconfigured.

**Importing history from a different chat platform (not Chatty→Chatty):** there's no migration tool for this either — historical conversations/tickets stay in the previous platform. What does carry over easily is the merchant's knowledge: export existing FAQs or macros from the old platform and import into Chatty via **FAQs → More actions → Import FAQs**, or add them as Q&As under **Training data → Knowledge base**. Offer to help set this up as part of onboarding if the merchant shares the content or page URL.

---

## Chat History via API

The **Chatty Public API does support pulling conversations and messages** — you can list a conversation's messages via the API. There are also **webhooks** (e.g. `customer_message`, `ai_response`) that push chats to your own server in near real time.

**API key generation and webhooks are Pro/Plus only** — on Free/Basic the merchant must upgrade to generate a key. See `faq_klaviyo` → *Chatty Public API & Webhooks*.

What is **not** available via the API is a **bulk full-conversation / date-range export** — for that, route the merchant to support, or use the **Zendesk** integration (all Chatty conversations are automatically saved as Zendesk tickets when marked resolved). The support team can also manually export transcripts.

---

## Conversation Summarize Button

Inbox conversations have a **summarize button** inside an open conversation that generates a quick summary of the chat so far, so a team member can catch up without reading the full thread.

**Stability fixed 20/08:** the button used to fail intermittently and surface a raw technical error message to the team member. As of 20/08, those failure cases are fixed, and if it still can't summarize for any reason, it now shows a plain "couldn't summarize" message instead of a technical error. If a merchant/teammate reports the summarize button erroring or not working from before this date, that's the known (now-fixed) issue — a fresh failure after 20/08 should be treated as new.

## Star Icon on Conversations

The **star icon** on a conversation indicates that the conversation is currently being handled by the **AI agent**.

---

## Where Chat Images and Files Are Stored

Images and files that customers send in chat are stored in the merchant's **Shopify Files**
(Shopify Admin → Content → Files). On the **Free plan** this is the only storage option, so
chat attachments will always appear there.

To store chat attachments in external storage instead of Shopify Files, upgrade to a paid plan.

## Finding the Inbox in Shopify Mobile Admin

On the Shopify mobile app, the Chatty Inbox is **not** in the app's "..." menu (that menu only
has Manage app, Get support, Pin, and Uninstall).

Tap the **hamburger menu next to the search field in the header**, then find **Inbox** under
the **Chatty** app.

## What the Inbox Search Bar Supports

The main **Inbox search bar** (top of the conversation list) matches on more than just the customer's name/email. As of **29/05**, it also matches:

- **Phone number**
- **Order number**
- **Conversation tag**

Results still combine with whatever **status/channel/assignee filters** are already active. This is the general search bar — it's different from **Custom Attribute Search** (see below), which searches on custom attribute values rather than these built-in fields.

## Cannot Find Messages in Inbox

1. **Check all tabs** — inbox tabs are **All, Your Inbox, Unassigned, Blocked**; also check the **Status** filter (Open, Resolved, Starred, Blocked, Unread) — conversations may be sitting under Unassigned or Resolved
2. **Check channel filter** — message may be from a different channel (email vs. web chat); use the channel filter to switch views
3. **If inbox shows error code** (e.g., "9 Failed Pre-conditioning") → clear browser cache, refresh the page; if error persists → escalate to TS with the error code
4. **If using search** → try browsing manually instead; search may miss recently received messages

---

## Customer Chatted But No Conversation Found

If a customer says they talked to Chatty but you can't locate the conversation:

- Anonymous chats appear under a **random/visitor name, not the customer's order email** — search by the **approximate date** rather than by email. Check every tab (Open, Resolved, Spam/Automated) and clear filters.
- If it genuinely never appears, it may be tied to the current **inbox-loading / 404 defect** (see "404 / Inbox-Crash" in the Others doc) — collect the customer email, approximate date/time, store URL and a screenshot, and escalate so the team can trace it server-side.
- Don't promise a conversation existed if it can't be located — some "the bot told my customer X" reports turn out to be email threads or other channels.

## Conversations Mixing Between Threads / Inbox Lagging

For stores with a very large volume of conversation data, the inbox can lag while fetching and rendering, sometimes requiring a page refresh to load the latest messages.

Cases where messages appear to **mix between different conversation threads** are treated as **high-priority and escalated to the dev team** for investigation. If a merchant experiences this, collect the affected **conversation IDs** and escalate so the team can investigate thoroughly.

---

## Mark All Conversations as Resolved

There is currently **no bulk "resolve all" button** in the inbox. Conversations must be resolved individually.

**Feature request:** This has been logged with the product team.

**For large volumes:** Contact support — the team may be able to help with a backend bulk resolve for your account.

---

## ⚠️ Bulk Conversation Delete — Also Permanently Deletes Contacts (as of 05/08)

As of **05/08**, Chatty supports **bulk deleting conversations** from the Inbox (selecting and deleting multiple conversations at once, rather than one at a time).

**Warning — this is destructive and irreversible:** bulk-deleting conversations does **not** just remove the conversation records. It also **permanently deletes the associated contact records** for every customer whose conversation was included in the bulk delete. There is no undo.

**Guidance for CS and the bot:**
- Do **not** suggest bulk conversation delete casually as a way to "clean up" the inbox (e.g. for spam or clutter) — it will wipe out real contact data along with it.
- Before recommending or confirming a bulk delete, make sure the merchant understands both the conversations **and** the linked contacts (profile, order history, tags/notes) will be gone permanently.
- Treat this the same as any other irreversible/destructive action — flag the risk clearly rather than walking through it like a routine cleanup step.

See `kb/faq/contacts.md` for how contact records and deletion work.

---

## Tagging Conversations

Conversations can be tagged manually (open a conversation → tag panel) and filtered on by tag. **Automatic tag assignment by keyword is not currently available** — every tag must be added manually per conversation. Log a request for keyword-based auto-tagging as a feature request.

## Custom Attribute Search

Conversations can be searched by **custom attribute values** — for example, searching for all conversations tagged with a "Pre-order" custom attribute.

**Limit:** a conversation can carry up to **50 custom attribute values**.

---

## Reopening a Resolved Conversation

Open the conversation from the **Resolved** tab — there is a **Reopen** button at the top. It moves the conversation back to the **Open** list.

Customers have no "Unresolve" control: a resolved conversation reopens on their side only when they send a new message, and after ~5 days of inactivity a new message starts a brand-new conversation instead.

See `faq_others` → *Reopening / Un-resolving a Conversation*.

---

## Customer Replies Go to Chatty Inbox

This is **expected behavior** for the email channel — all replies are threaded in Chatty's inbox for unified management.

**If the merchant wants replies to go directly to their email client:**
1. Go to **Channels → Email → Email sender** settings → check the **Reply-To** field
2. Set the Reply-To address to the merchant's actual support email
3. Customers' replies will then arrive at both Chatty and the configured email client

> Explain to merchants that the Chatty inbox is the intended management hub. The Reply-To field workaround is for merchants who prefer their traditional email workflow.

---

## Anonymous Conversations With Pre-Chat Form Enabled

Two features can bypass the pre-chat form:

1. **AI Product Page Assistant** — when embedded on product pages, customers can chat immediately without providing their email. The system prioritizes fast support.
2. **Proactive Chat** — when enabled, customers can reply to the proactive chat bubble without filling the pre-chat form first.

**Solution:** If you want to enforce info collection for all conversations, disable the AI Product Page Assistant embed and/or Proactive Chat features.

## Suggest Reply (Beta)

A **"Suggest reply"** capability is in **Beta**: the AI drafts a response that an agent reviews before sending (AI generates → human reviews → human presses **Send**), so it does not auto-send to your company email.

- It's being rolled out to **select merchants** — if a merchant wants in, log their interest.
- Known Beta limitations: the drafted-email **formatting/spacing** still needs polish, and suggestions **aren't always accurate** (e.g. it suggested "in stock" when the item was out of stock).
- Until it's GA, keep the AI **off** for company email if every email could get an incorrect auto-reply, and use it on **live chat** where an agent can supervise.

# AI Wrong Responses

## AI Answer Style Changed After 20/08 (Answer Engine Migration)

**As of 20/08**, every store's live chat runs on Chatty's new AI answer engine (an independent, always-on service — internally "ai-vm"), replacing the old engine that only ran for a pilot group of stores. Functionally the AI's tools (product lookup, order lookup, FAQ lookup, discount lookup, etc.) are unchanged — this is an infrastructure swap, not a feature change, and it also fixes the old "stuck AI" failure mode where a dropped customer connection could silently lose an in-progress AI answer with no record of it.

**If a merchant reports the AI "sounds different" after 20/08** — different tone, different response length, or picking different details than before — **don't immediately treat it as a bug.** This engine migration is a plausible cause. Collect the specific example (conversation ID, exact question, what changed) and flag it to the product team for review rather than asserting it's broken or promising a fix.

> **How this file resolves things now:** every case below follows the same pattern — collect the
> full details from the merchant first, run a `<consult_ts>` diagnostic check, and read the result
> when it arrives in a later turn.
> - **TS confirms a clear cause/fix** → answer the merchant yourself, in your own words, from that
>   result. Stay in the conversation.
> - **TS is not confident, needs more digging, or confirms a real defect that needs dev/team work** →
>   create a `<ticket mode="async">` with everything collected + the TS note, tell the merchant
>   you've flagged it to the team and will follow up here, and **stay in the conversation** —
>   never go silent on the merchant while a ticket is open.
>
> A few sections are pure feature requests or account-level config asks with nothing to diagnose
> (e.g. disabling add-to-cart account-wide, deep variant links) — those skip the TS consult and go
> straight to a ticket, same as before.

## AI Not Responding at All

Ask the merchant to check in this order:

1. **Verify AI agent is enabled** — toggle must be ON in AI agent settings
2. **Check plan's AI conversation limit:**
   - Free plan = 50 conversations/month (resets monthly) — when hit, AI pauses until the next cycle
   - Paid plans = monthly quota; when quota is exhausted AI stops until billing reset
   - Guide merchant to upgrade or wait for monthly reset if limit is the cause
3. **Check training data is added and synced** — AI cannot reply if no data sources are active
4. **Ensure Live Chat block is enabled** — go to **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Blocks** → enable **Live chat**. This step applies to **Legacy chatbox** only; a store on **AI Mode** has no Live chat block (it opens straight into chat), so skip it there

> ⚠️ Check plan limits **first** — this is the most common cause for AI suddenly stopping.

**If none of the above resolves it**, this exact scenario is handled by `flows/ai_not_responding.md`
— follow that flow's collect → consult_ts → ticket sequence rather than acting from here.

## AI Hallucinating / Over-Promising

**Step 1 — Collect from the merchant:**
- Conversation ID, or customer name/email in that chat
- What the customer asked
- What the AI promised or said (exact wrong answer)
- What the correct response should have been
- Whether this has happened more than once / with multiple customers

**Step 2 — Guide merchant to check Review Sources (do this while consulting TS):**
- Open the conversation → find the wrong AI reply → click **Review Sources**
- Ask: *"Does any source shown mention refunds/returns, or is there no source at all?"*
- No source shown = likely hallucination; source shown = training data may contain incorrect info

**Step 3 — Consult TS:**

`<consult_ts type="diagnostic" summary="AI hallucinated a refund/return promise. Conversation ID/customer: [id/customer]. Khách hỏi: [question]. AI đã hứa/nói: [wrong promise]. Đáp án đúng: [correct response]. Lặp lại nhiều lần/nhiều KH: [yes/no]. Review Sources: [findings]."/>`

**Step 4 — Act on the result:**
- TS confirms and gives the correct handling → answer the merchant directly from it.
- TS not confident / confirms a real gap → create a ticket:

`<ticket mode="async" priority="high" subject="AI hứa nhầm refund/return với khách" summary="AI hallucinate 1 lời hứa refund/return.
- Conversation ID/customer: [id/customer]
- Khách hỏi: [question]
- AI đã hứa/nói: [wrong promise]
- Đáp án đúng: [correct response]
- Lặp lại nhiều lần/nhiều KH: [yes/no]
- Review Sources: [findings]
- TS note: [kết quả TS, nếu có]"/>`

Priority `high` — a wrong refund/return promise can already be relied on by the customer.

**Immediately suggest a temporary instruction to prevent recurrence**, regardless of the ticket:
- Go to **AI agent → Scenarios** → add scenario with keywords: "refund", "return", "replacement"
- Instruction: *"Ask the customer for photos and direct them to support email instead of promising any action."*

> Known limitation — the AI may over-promise based on general knowledge if not explicitly restricted via instructions.

## AI Mentioned a Wrong Discount or Promotion

**Step 1 — Collect from the merchant:**
- Conversation ID, or customer name/email in that chat
- What the customer asked
- What discount the AI mentioned (e.g. "30% off", specific promo code)
- Whether this discount exists or has existed anywhere (active promo, old campaign, etc.)
- Whether this has happened more than once / with multiple customers

**Note:** Chatty automatically syncs promotion data from the store. The AI may be pulling a real (but outdated or unintended) discount from synced data — this is not always a hallucination.

**Step 2 — Guide merchant to check Review Sources (do this while consulting TS):**
- Open the conversation → find the wrong AI reply → click **Review Sources**
- Ask: *"Is there a source shown that mentions this discount? Or no source at all?"*
- Source shown with discount info = synced data issue; no source = hallucination
