## AI Misreads Store Page Layout — Comparison Tables, Strikethrough Pricing

**Known limitation:** the AI reads page content as text and does not reliably interpret visual formatting like **strikethrough**, or which **column/row** a table value belongs to. Two recurring patterns:

- **Comparison tables (e.g. a spec table with checkmarks per product column):** if a merchant's page compares multiple products/models in a table, the AI can attribute a checkmark or feature to the wrong column/product — it read the row text correctly but matched it to the wrong product name.
- **Strikethrough / "compare at" pricing:** when a price on the page has strikethrough styling (e.g. a crossed-out MSRP shown next to the real price, or a "Deposit-only" label that isn't carried over as plain text), the AI can't detect the strikethrough and may read the crossed-out number as if it were the active, full price.

**What to do:**
1. Confirm via **Review Sources** on the wrong reply — the AI is usually quoting real page content, just misattributed or missing its formatting context, not fabricating a number.
2. Give the merchant/customer the accurate figure or comparison for that conversation.
3. **Workaround for the merchant:** add an explicit Q&A under **AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base** stating the correct fact in plain text (e.g. "$6,999 is a deposit-only price, not the full MSRP" or "Feature X is available on the Pro model, not the base model"). A plain-text Q&A gives the AI an unambiguous source instead of the raw page layout.
4. This is a **known AI limitation with visual formatting/table structure**, not a data-sync issue — don't send the merchant to re-sync products or pages, that will not fix it.

## AI Add-to-Cart Issues

**There is NO merchant self-serve add-to-cart toggle.** Add-to-cart is automatic behavior of the AI product assistant — when a customer asks in chat, the AI adds the item to the cart. Do not tell the merchant to look for a toggle under AI agent → Settings; no such option exists there. If the AI is not adding items, it is a theme-compatibility or product/variant issue, not a setting — diagnose below.

**If the merchant wants add-to-cart turned OFF entirely** (e.g. a store whose goal is appointment bookings rather than direct sales, or the AI is adding to cart against instructions on ambiguous replies): this can't be self-served, but the backend team can disable AI add-to-cart features for that account on request — this is an account-config request, not a bug, so no TS consult is needed. - Lý do: [reason]"/>`

# Online Hours

## Online Hours Overview

Online hours lets you define your working hours, break times, and holidays so customers know when to expect live support.

> Note: Online/offline status only works when the **Live chat** block is turned on at **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Blocks** (Legacy chatbox only).

## How to Set Up Online Hours

Go to **Settings → General → Chat availability → Manage**

**Working hours:**
- **24 hours / 7 days**: Always available for chat
- **Custom time**: Set specific hours per day of the week

**Break time:** Toggle on to add short offline periods within your working hours

**Holiday:** Toggle on to mark specific days as fully offline

**Time zone:** Select the timezone for your support team so availability displays correctly to customers

**First auto-reply:** Toggle on to send an automatic first message when a customer starts a chat
- **Online message**: Shown during working hours (e.g. "Thank you for reaching out. We'll be with you in a moment")
- **Offline message**: Shown outside working hours (e.g. "We are currently offline. We will respond as soon as possible during our next business hours")

Click **Save**. The chatbox preview on the right lets you check how it looks for online and offline states before saving.

## Holiday Hours and Chats Sent Outside Working Hours (fixed 24/08)

Two related fixes landed 24/08:

- **Holiday no longer shows the regular weekly hours.** Before this date, a day marked as a holiday could still display the store's normal weekly working hours to customers instead of showing the store as offline/closed. If a merchant reports "AI still shows regular hours on a holiday," that describes the old bug — a fresh report from after 24/08 should be treated as new.
- **Chats sent outside working hours still reach the AI.** Before this date, a chat that came in outside working hours could go unanswered instead of being routed to the AI. Now, a chat started outside working hours is still passed to the AI to answer (subject to the merchant's own Human Handover offline-behavior settings — see `faq_human-handover` → *Offline Behavior*). If a merchant reports "no one answers customers outside our hours," check this fix first before assuming a config issue.

## Holiday Message Persists After the Toggle Is Turned Off (leftover Knowledge base entry)

The Holiday toggle above only controls the store's working-hours status — it does **not** touch anything a merchant separately typed into training data. If a merchant manually added a holiday-closure notice as a **Knowledge base / training data entry** (e.g. to give the AI extra context during the closure), turning the Holiday toggle back off does **not** automatically remove that entry. The AI can keep citing the old holiday message from its knowledge base even though the toggle shows off.

If a merchant reports the AI still mentioning a holiday that's already ended, check **AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base** for a leftover manually-added entry and remove or update it directly — this is a separate check from confirming the Holiday toggle itself is off.

# FAQs Block

## FAQs Block Overview

A FAQs block lets you display a specific set of FAQs on any page of your store — for example, showing product-specific questions only on the relevant product page.

You can create multiple FAQs blocks with different questions for different products, collections, or pages.

## Showing FAQs Inside the Chatbox Itself (Not a FAQs Block)

If a merchant wants FAQ questions to show **inside the chat widget itself** — not on a specific storefront page — that is a **different feature from FAQs blocks** below. Don't point them to FAQs block for this.

1. Go to **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Blocks**, turn on the **FAQs** block (blocks exist on **Legacy chatbox** only — **AI Mode** surfaces FAQ content as **Commonly Asked** instead)
2. To control which questions appear first when the chatbox opens, go to **FAQs → Manage FAQs** and mark the desired questions as **Featured** — featured questions show on the first page of the chatbox

**FAQs blocks** (below) are for showing FAQs embedded on specific **storefront pages** (product pages, homepage, collection, cart, blog, or a custom URL) — they render on the page itself, not inside the chat conversation.

## Showing Different FAQs on Different Products

To give each product (or group of products) its own set of FAQs on the storefront,
use **FAQs blocks** — this works with or without the AI agent, and does not require
the AI agent at all.

1. Go to **FAQs** → **FAQs block** → **Add block**
2. Click **Browse** and select the questions for this group of products
3. Under display condition, tick **Product pages** and choose:
   - **By collection** — show this block only on products in a given collection
   - **By tag** — show this block only on products carrying a given tag
4. **Save**, then add the block to the product template in the theme editor
   (**Add section** → **Chatty FAQs block** → paste the Block ID)
5. Repeat: create one block per collection/tag, each with its own questions

There's no limit on the number of blocks, so a store can have as many product-specific
FAQ sets as it needs.

> This is a **storefront display** feature and is separate from **AI agent → Training
> data**, which teaches the AI to answer in chat. Adding FAQs to a block does not
> require the AI agent to be active. It is also separate from the **chatbox FAQs block**
> described above — that one shows inside the chat widget, not on a storefront page.

## How to Set Up a FAQs Block

1. Go to **FAQs** → **FAQs block**
2. Click **Add block** (if no blocks exist yet, the page shows an empty state with this button)
3. Set **General** information:
   - **Block name**: Internal name to identify this block (visible to admin only)
   - **Heading & Subheading**: Text shown in the block
4. Click **Browse** and select the FAQ questions to show
   - Turn on "Don't categorize FAQs" to show all questions in a flat list without category headers
5. Set display condition — choose where to show the block. **The Display condition section is collapsed by default — click it to expand before you can tick anything underneath.** There are two groups (you must select at least one value in whichever group you tick):
   - **Product pages** — show on product pages: **All** product pages, **By collection**, or **By tag**
   - **Specific pages** — show on chosen pages: **Homepage**, **Collection**, **Cart**, **Blog**, or a **Custom URL**

   (The old single "All pages" option has been replaced by these two groups so you can target the exact pages you need. Use **Go to theme** to open any page in your selection and place the block there.)
6. Customize appearance:
   - Heading size and alignment
   - Card corner radius
   - Colors
7. Click **Save**
8. Copy the **Block ID**
9. Go to your **Theme editor**:
   - Navigate to the page where you want to add the block
   - Click **Add section** → Search for **Chatty FAQs block** → Add it
   - Paste the Block ID in the settings
10. Click **Save** in the theme editor

You can also add the block using code: Go to **FAQs block code** → **Copy** → Add the HTML to your website's code.

---

## Auto-Generating FAQs from Store Pages (Sync Store Page → Add Q&A)

To quickly populate FAQs without writing them by hand, use **AI agent → Training data → Knowledge base → Sync Store Page → Add Q&A**. The system scans your store pages (return policy, shipping policy, etc.) and **auto-generates ~15 common Q&As** you can review, edit, and add to the AI's knowledge base.

This is a fast way to seed both the AI's training data and your FAQ content from existing store policies.

---

## Managing FAQs Blocks

In the FAQs block tab, you can:
- View all blocks with details (Block ID, name, number of FAQs, display conditions, status)
- Edit or delete blocks
- Create as many blocks as needed — **there's no limit**

There is no limit on the number of FAQs blocks you can create. Create separate blocks for each product or collection as needed.

To reuse the same FAQ in multiple blocks, include it when selecting questions for each block you create. The same FAQ question can appear in multiple blocks by using the same Block ID.

6. Click **Create** → copy the key → paste into Chatty

Yes — the Chatty Public API supports:

# DFY Setup — Qualify, Collect Input & Hand the Job to the Team (via ticket)

> **Bot's role in DFY:** The bot does NOT set anything up itself. For "Done-For-You" (DFY) setup, our **CS/TS team (a human) does the actual setup**. The bot's job is to (1) give a quick self-serve guide, (2) recognize when the merchant wants the team to do it, (3) collect the input the team needs, then (4) hand the job over by creating a **ticket** with a `<ticket mode="async" ...>` tag. Internal SOP — ticket labels, SLA, module checklists — is handled by the team, not the bot, and is intentionally not in this knowledge base.

> **Ticket, NOT escalation.** DFY work is picked up from the ticket board, so the handoff is always a ticket and **you stay in the conversation** — keep answering the merchant, keep them updated, and never go silent after the ticket. Do **not** emit `<escalate>` for a DFY setup. The only exception: the merchant explicitly asks to talk to a real person → then (and only then) emit `<escalate reason="..."/>` as well.


## Overview

When a merchant says **"I need help on setup [AI agent / FAQs / Chatbox]"** — or anything like "can you set it up for me", "do it for me", or replies **"yes"** to a free setup offer — the request is ambiguous between two paths:

- **(A) Self-serve** — they want a step-by-step guide to do it themselves → bot answers, no ticket.
- **(B) Done-For-You (DFY)** — they want our team to set it up for them, or they tried and got stuck → bot collects input, then creates the ticket for the team.

## Golden Rule — Guide first, qualify, collect, then ticket

1. **Give the self-serve step-by-step guide FIRST** (most merchants can do it themselves — see the per-feature chunks below).
2. **Then ask one qualifying question** that makes clear the team does it all and it's free: *"Would you like to set this up yourself, or have our team handle the full setup for you — free of charge? They'll build it to fit your store, and you can adjust anything afterwards."*
3. **Hand the job to the team (DFY) ONLY when:**
   - Merchant clearly wants the **team to do it for them**, OR
   - Merchant **already tried the steps and it still doesn't work**, OR
   - Merchant is on a **paid plan / high-value (high GMV)** asking for hands-on help.
4. **Collect the input the team needs BEFORE creating the ticket** (see per-feature chunks). Ask for what's still missing, a couple of questions per turn, never dump the whole list at once. The ticket is created **once, when the intake is complete** — not at the first "yes".
5. **To hand off:** confirm the collected info back to the merchant in your own words, set a warm expectation, then append the `<ticket>` block at the very end of the reply (invisible to the customer).
   - `modules="…"` tells the system which module(s) the job covers: `ai_agent`, `chatbox`, `faqs` (comma-separated when the merchant asked for more than one). Always set it.
   - You do **not** write the ticket title, status or the team's checklist — the system fills those in the team's standard DFY format automatically.
   - The body is the internal note: first line is a short headline, then **every collected field on its own `- Field: value` line**.
   - Keep every exact name, greeting, email, URL, phone number, hour, preference, boundary, notification method, handover path, and order/after-sales behaviour **verbatim** as the merchant wrote it (do not translate their greeting or brand words).
   - **Always close the tag** with `</ticket>`. Never leave an empty `<ticket>` and never use `<escalate>` for the setup job itself.

> **⚠️ Minimum intake gate — the system BLOCKS a ticket that is too thin.** For the AI agent and Chatbox intakes the ticket may only be created once you have all the answers from the merchant; for the FAQ paths the one required field for that path (collaborator code / FAQ source) must be resolved first. This is enforced in code, not on trust: if your `<ticket>` note carries fewer real fields than that, **no ticket is created at all** — the job never reaches the team and you have to keep collecting. Collect first, ticket after.
>
> **What counts as a "real answer".** A field is real only when it carries something the merchant actually gave you: a name, a greeting, an email, an hour range, a preference in their own words. These never count:
> - the store domain (the system attaches it by itself);
> - `not specified`, `n/a`, `none`, `unknown`, or an empty value;
> - a bare `yes` / `ok` / `sure` / `done` / `thanks` in reply to an **open** question — that is not an answer, that is a merchant who did not read or did not understand. Ask again, one question at a time, in simpler words.
>
> **Never invent a field to hold a non-answer.** Lines like `- Customer response to greeting question: yes` are forbidden: they make the ticket look filled while telling the team nothing.
>
> **Never write a bare `yes` / `no` as a field value — write the decision it expresses.** A yes/no to a closed question IS a real answer, but the team cannot act on the word alone, and the system does not count it. Spell it out:
> - ❌ `- Order lookup: yes` → ✅ `- Order lookup: yes — the assistant may look up order status directly`
> - ❌ `- Order lookup: no` → ✅ `- Order lookup: no — order questions always go to the merchant`
> - ❌ `- Availability: yes` → ✅ `- Availability: always on, 24/7`

> **"Do it for me" is a YES to DFY, not a refusal to answer.** *"I want you to do it for me"*, *"just set it up"*, *"can you do it"*, *"yes please set it up"*, *"I want the team to handle it"* — these are the merchant **choosing the DFY path** (Step 3). They are the reason you START the intake, never a reason to end it. Confirm warmly, then ask the intake questions.

> **Check the timing before concluding "they didn't answer".** If the merchant's message lands within a few seconds of your question, they had no time to read it — they are replying to your *previous* message. Treat your question as still unanswered, ask it again lightly, and never record it as `not specified`.

> The bot never claims to have set anything up itself. It says the **team** will set it up. Phrasing like *"I'll pass this to our team who'll set this up for you"* — never *"I've set it up"*.

> **How to collect input (all flows): ONE question per turn.** Ask a single question, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Two questions in one message is exactly how you end up with a single "yes" that answers neither — it has happened and it produced an unworkable ticket. Keep it light and conversational, ask only for what is still missing, and confirm back before creating the ticket. The wording below is written to be sent to the merchant almost as-is.

## After the ticket is created — you keep running

- Tell the merchant the team will complete the setup **within 12–24 hours** and **updates will come here in this chat**.
- **Stay in the conversation.** Answer anything else they ask (how-to, pricing, other features) as usual.
- If they add more setup details later, **don't open a second ticket** — reply normally and append another `<ticket mode="async" ...>` block with just the new information; the system attaches it to the same ticket automatically.
- If they ask "how long?", tell them the team completes it within 12–24 hours. If they ask "any news?", answer from what you know about the job's status; never invent progress and never say it's done unless you've been told it is.
- Only if they explicitly ask for a human ("talk to someone", "real person") → add `<escalate reason="merchant asks for a human during DFY setup"/>`.

## Flow — Setup AI agent

### Step 1 — Give the self-serve guide first

> Happy to help you set up your AI agent! Here's how to get started:
> 1. **AI agent → Training data** — add training data (Products, Collections, Discounts, Markets, Knowledge base).
> 2. **AI agent → Instructions** — add custom instructions for how the AI should respond.
> 3. **Test AI → Test now** — test the responses before going live.

### Step 2 — Qualify (ask at the end of Step 1)

> Would you like to set this up yourself, or have our team handle the full setup for you — free of charge? They'll train your AI assistant to fit your store, and you can adjust anything afterwards.

### Step 3 — Branch

- **Self-serve / just a question** → answer follow-ups from `ai-training__*` chunks. **No ticket.**
- **Wants team to do it / tried & stuck / paid plan asking for hands-on help** → Step 4.

### Step 4 — Collect AI input, then create the ticket

The team needs these ten answers before they can train the AI well. **Send exactly one question per turn** — one question mark per message, then wait for the reply. Never join two questions with "Also…", "and", or a second "?": the merchant answers only the last one and the first field is lost for good. Ask only for what is still missing, and skip anything they already told you.

1. **Goals & pain point** — When you picture your AI assistant on your website, what would you most like it to take off your plate — answering FAQs, recommending products, tracking orders, handling returns, or covering while you're away?
2. **Current support team** — Do you have anyone handling customer support at the moment?
   - *Next turn, only if they do:* What hours does your team usually cover?
3. **Availability** — Would you like the assistant online 24/7, or only stepping in when your team is away?
4. **Assistant name** — What should we call your assistant?
5. **Greeting** — How would you like it to greet your customers?
6. **Notifications** — Where would you like to be notified when a new chat comes in — web push, email, or both?
   - *Next turn, only if they chose email:* Which email address should those alerts go to?
7. **Brand, products & tone** — Tell me a bit about your brand and what you sell.
   - *Next turn:* How would you like your assistant to sound — warm and friendly, polite, or more polished?
8. **Boundaries** — Are there any topics you'd rather it didn't handle, so I can set the right boundaries?
9. **Routing to a human** — When a customer needs a real person — a general question or an after-sales request like a return, refund or order change — how would you like it routed to you: (1) transfer the chat straight into your Chatty inbox, (2) collect their details and follow up by email, or (3) show your contact info so they can reach you directly?
10. **Order lookup** — Would you like the assistant to look up a customer's order status directly, or should that always come to you?

Also note internally: **where exactly they're stuck** and **what they've already tried** (if they came in stuck).

**When the merchant brushes the questions off** ("just do it", "whatever you think is best", "you decide", "yes" to everything, or they simply stop answering) — you do **not** get to ticket an empty intake, and there is no shortcut: a note below the gate is rejected by the system. Do this instead:

1. **First brush-off** → reassure them the team handles everything, then ask **one** question again in simpler words. Pick the single most valuable missing field (the assistant's name).
2. **Second brush-off** → stop asking open questions and **offer concrete defaults they only have to agree to**. Convey the idea in your own words, in the merchant's language: the team takes care of everything, and so it fits their store you suggest the assistant handles general customer questions and covers conversations when the merchant is away, introduces itself as their store assistant, assumes there's no dedicated support team yet so it stays available around the clock, sends new-chat alerts to the email on their account, and routes anything about orders, returns or refunds straight to them — then ask for one simple confirmation.
3. **They agree to the defaults** ("sounds good", "ok do that", "yes please") → those defaults are now **their answers**. Write them into the note as **concrete values**, never as `not specified`:
   - `- Goals/pain point: general customer support — answering FAQs and covering conversations when the merchant is away (merchant accepted our suggestion)`
   - `- Current support team: no dedicated team specified — AI to stay online 24/7 as default (merchant accepted our suggestion)`
   - `- Assistant name: <store name> assistant (merchant accepted our suggestion)`
   - `- Availability/hours: always on, 24/7 (merchant accepted our suggestion)`
   - `- Notifications: email on the store account (merchant accepted our suggestion)`
   - `- Human handover: orders, returns and refunds routed straight to the merchant (merchant accepted our suggestion)`

   That clears the gate honestly, and the team can see exactly what was agreed versus what was assumed.
4. **They keep refusing to engage at all** → keep answering whatever else they ask, keep the chat warm, and leave the intake open. Do **not** create a ticket the team cannot work, and do **not** escalate: every blocked attempt already drops an internal note in this chat, so the team can see the case waiting.

**All ten answers must be resolved** (real answer or accepted default) **before creating the ticket** — do not create it while any field is still open. If the merchant keeps skipping one, go back to the brush-off ladder above for that field instead of settling for a partial ticket.

Then confirm back and create the ticket:

> Perfect — I'll pass this to our team and they'll set up and train your AI assistant for you within 12–24 hours, then send it back for your review. I'll keep you posted right here.
>

## Common Issues

- **Chatbox not showing on store**: Check that **Display chatbox on your store** is on (the master toggle at the top of the **Chatbox** page), app embed is enabled in the Shopify theme editor, and display rules aren't excluding the page (**Chatbox → Shared chatbox settings → Display rules**).
- **AI not responding**: Verify the AI agent is turned on, training data is synced, and the AI has enough content to answer from. On **Legacy chatbox**, also check the **Live chat** block at **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Blocks**; **AI Mode** has no blocks, so skip that step there.
- **Email channel not connecting (Outlook)**: Organization's Outlook settings may block automatic email forwarding. Contact IT admin to allow email forwarding.
- **Online status not showing**: the **Contact** block must be enabled — **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Blocks → Contact** (Legacy chatbox only; **AI Mode** has no blocks).
- **WhatsApp not connecting**: Ensure you have a Business Facebook page, WhatsApp Business account linked to it, and admin access to both accounts.
- **Translation not showing on store**: Website must support the language first. In Shopify Admin > Settings > Languages, add and publish the language before enabling it in Chatty.
- **AI recommending wrong products**: Check the Smart recommendations collections at **AI agent → Skills → Shopping → Smart recommendations**. Disable smart sync if auto-selected products aren't relevant. Manually curate product lists.
- **FAQ page not showing after uninstall/reinstall**: After uninstalling, Chatty's code may remain disabled. Check Shopify Admin > Online Store > Pages for orphaned FAQ pages.
- **Order tracking not working**: On **Legacy chatbox**, ensure the **Order tracking** block is on at **Chatbox → Chatbox mode → Legacy chatbox → General → Blocks**. On **AI Mode** there is no block — the customer asks the AI to track an order in chat. Verify Shopify order tracking info is properly set up.
- **Products not appearing in AI training**: Only published, in-stock products are trained. Products sync daily at 00:00 UTC. Check product count against plan limit.

# AI stays silent — no reply at all to customers (different from replying wrongly)

The AI produces **nothing**. A customer writes and no answer comes back. That is a different
failure from the AI answering incorrectly, and it has a different set of causes: it is almost
always a gate that is switched off somewhere, not a defect in the model.

Do not confuse it with:

- the AI answering **something wrong** — that is the wrong-answer flow,
- the bot talking **over a human agent** — that is the handover flow,
- the whole widget being invisible on the storefront — then customers cannot write at all, and
  that is the widget flow. Check which one they mean before starting.

## Before Step 1 — Check the timing against the 02/09 auto-recovery fix

Since **02/09**, a background safety net automatically re-answers messages that got dropped mid-pipeline
(the customer's message came in but nothing was ever sent back) — this is separate from the 20/08
ai-vm engine migration (see `case_ai-wrong-responses` → *AI Answer Style Changed After 20/08*), and
covers cases that engine migration didn't. There's also an internal tool that re-scans old stuck
conversations from before this fix.

If a merchant reports "customer got no answer" from **before 02/09**, this may already be self-resolved
— ask if it's still happening on a fresh message before treating it as an active issue. A report of
genuine silence on a message sent **after 02/09** is not expected and should still go through the
collect → consult_ts → ticket flow below as normal.

## Step 1 — Collect the four facts TS needs to replay it

1. **Where they tested** — the live storefront, or the Test AI section inside the app. These are
   the same pipeline but different context, and the answer changes the diagnosis.
2. **The exact question that got no reply**, verbatim.
3. **Which channel** — online store widget, WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, email.
4. **When it last worked**, and whether it is every message or only some.

A screenshot of the chat covers most of this at once and is the easiest thing to send — ask for it
when they have not already.

## Step 2 — Hand to TS for inspection

`<consult_ts type="diagnostic" summary="AI im lặng, không trả lời gì. Test ở: <live storefront / Test AI>. Câu hỏi không được trả lời (nguyên văn): <...>. Kênh: <...>. Lần cuối còn chạy: <...>. Mọi tin hay chỉ một số: <...>"/>`

TS can read every gate directly, so do not walk the merchant through a settings checklist first.

## Step 3 — When the TS diagnosis comes back

Reply in the merchant's language. The causes that explain nearly all of these, and what each one
means for the merchant:

- **The AI assistant is switched off** — the widget still works for live chat, but nothing answers
  automatically. Chatty → AI agent.
- **The channel is not enabled for automatic replies** — the AI answers on the online store but not
  on WhatsApp or Messenger, because that channel was never added to auto-answer.
- **The conversation quota is used up** — the AI stops replying once the plan's AI conversations run
  out. This is not a defect, and merchants almost never guess it. Say it plainly and point at the
  usage figure.
- **The conversation was resolved or a human took it over** — the AI does not speak in a resolved or
  human-handled conversation until it is reopened.
- **A runtime error in the pipeline** — this one is a real defect.

Never mention TS, traces, spans, or internal field names.

## Step 4 — Create the ticket only when TS confirms a defect

`<ticket mode="async" priority="high" subject="<tiêu đề tiếng Việt, dưới 55 ký tự>" summary="AI không trả lời khách.
- Test ở: <live storefront / Test AI>
- Câu hỏi không được trả lời (nguyên văn): <...>
- Kênh: <...>
- Lần cuối còn chạy: <...>
- Mọi tin hay chỉ một số: <...>
- TS chẩn đoán: <root cause từ note>
- Evidence: <error span / cấu hình TS đọc được>"/>`

Priority `high` — im lặng nghĩa là khách đang bị bỏ rơi, không ai biết.

Write the ticket in Vietnamese. Never put a `>` character inside the summary.

## Never create a ticket when

- The AI assistant, the channel, or a knowledge source is switched off — that is a setting.
- The AI conversation quota is exhausted — that is the plan, not a bug.
- A human agent already joined the conversation, or it was resolved — the AI is meant to stay quiet.
- The merchant is testing outside their configured working hours with live chat handover on.
- The complaint is actually a wrong or unhelpful answer rather than silence.
